actions: initiates/assists glenohumeral abduction (first ~15deg, then throughout with deltoid)
stabilizes humeral head in glenoid (rotator cuff force-couple)

functional_compartments.name: Anterior compartment (larger, more pennate)

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: central tendon endplate band, short highly-pennate fascicles

functional_compartments.function_note: Larger anterior compartment generates most of the abduction-initiation torque; documented as mechanically/architecturally distinct from the posterior compartment.
functional_compartments.source: Roh MS et al. (2000) Clin Orthop Relat Res 375:242-249 (supraspinatus anterior/posterior compartmentalization); Kim SY et al. cadaveric partition studies

functional_compartments.name: Posterior compartment (smaller)
functional_compartments.function_note: Smaller posterior compartment; contributes proportionally less PCSA.
functional_compartments.source: Roh MS et al. (2000) Clin Orthop Relat Res 375:242-249

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity musculoskeletal model; Roh MS, Wang VM, April EW, Pollock RG, Bigliani LU, Flatow EL (2000) Clin Orthop Relat Res 375:242-249

trigger_points.location_description: Medial belly point, in the mid-fossa of the supraspinous fossa, deep to trapezius
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Deep ache in the mid-deltoid region, spreading down the lateral arm and forearm and often concentrating at the lateral epicondyle; occasionally to the wrist.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Felt during abduction and when carrying weights at the side; may produce a dull ache at rest.
trigger_points.notes: One of two classic belly points described for this muscle (with the lateral belly point below); an occasional third tender point is described near the musculotendinous/tendon zone at the greater tuberosity, without a separately characterised referral pattern.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded shoulder muscle reference document (Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)

trigger_points.location_description: Lateral belly point, just medial to the acromion, deep to trapezius
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Deep ache in the mid-deltoid region, spreading down the lateral arm and forearm and often concentrating at the lateral epicondyle; occasionally to the wrist.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Felt during abduction and when carrying weights at the side; may produce a dull ache at rest.
trigger_points.notes: Second of the two classic belly points (with the medial belly point above).
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded shoulder muscle reference document (Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)
